picks.title: A properties panel and annotations, now in Figma Make
picks.excerpt: Figma Make adds a visual properties panel and annotations, letting designers edit AI-generated output directly and hand off intent to code without re-prompting. A real feature release tightening the design-to-code loop in Figma's AI builder.
picks.rationale: Concrete Figma Make feature release that changes the edit/handoff loop designers use tomorrow — highest actionability in the pool.

picks.title: Perplexity diverges with color: building data color schemes with generative AI
picks.excerpt: A hands-on look at using generative AI (via Perplexity) to construct diverging data-visualization color schemes and palette tokens. A concrete workflow for folding AI into the systematic, accessibility-sensitive craft of color-system design.
picks.rationale: Hands-on, reproducible method for generating accessible color-scheme tokens with AI — actionable craft, and adds category diversity beyond workflow.

picks.title: From Tinder and Reddit to Amazon, unwanted AI images are freaking people out
picks.excerpt: Across Amazon, Tinder and Reddit, products are now silently generating or editing users' photos with AI by default, with opt-out left to the user. A pointed product-design and UX-consent lesson as generative image AI gets pushed into mainstream interfaces without asking.
picks.rationale: A sharp product-design/consent case study on default-on generative AI across major apps — a UX-ethics signal designers should weigh in their own patterns.

picks.title: AI fluency isn't the finish line
picks.excerpt: Ninety percent of product builders call AI skills essential, but Figma argues teams are optimizing for the wrong ones and reframes what design craft means past basic tool fluency. A pointed take on how AI is reshaping the skills a design org actually needs.
picks.rationale: Credible Figma-authored reframing of which AI-era design skills actually matter — shapes how teams train and hire, backed by survey data.

picks.title: Creative technologists are moving from the margins to the center
picks.excerpt: Once a fringe job title, creative technology is becoming a core capability inside modern product teams as AI collapses the gap between design and code. Argues the designer-who-builds is shifting from novelty to default operating model for AI-era design orgs.
picks.rationale: Frames the designer-who-builds as the new default operating model — a role-shift insight for how design teams staff and structure around AI.
